text:
Ana: FYI ran a quick perf pass on canary after the kernel-sampler change. p99 for streaming chat jumped on small flows.
Devon: can you paste the numbers and timeline?
Ana: baseline (before sampler): streaming p99 ~ 210ms, p95 ~ 85ms. after sampler: p99 ~ 680ms, p95 ~ 95ms. non-streaming completions unchanged.
Shaun: sampler should only change kernel selection for larger mb sizes. are small microbatches being routed to the sampler path by mistake?
Ana: trace excerpt:
```
[2026-03-13 14:12:03] req-id=abc123 handshake 12ms
[2026-03-13 14:12:03] req-id=abc123 kernel-sampler decision wait 320ms
[2026-03-13 14:12:03] req-id=abc123 kv-prefetch miss 5ms
[2026-03-13 14:12:03] req-id=abc123 execute kernel-optimized 18ms
```
Marta: that 320ms wait looks like the sampler queuing microbatches until a threshold is met. streaming wants tiny mb sizes (1-2) so queuing creates tail.
Devon: sampler currently waits for mb_target=4 before picking kernel. for streaming flows mb_size=1, so they now sometimes wait for extra arrivals before kernel decision.
Ana: we saw this pattern: if a chat flow is single-turn, it waits ~300-400ms trying to coalesce, then falls back but too late for p99.
Tim: non-streaming completions usually have mbsize>=8 so they benefit from sampled kernels — that explains why completions unaffected.
Shaun: two obvious mitigation options: 1) short-circuit sampler for flows flagged as streaming, 2) per-flow hysteresis so if waiting > X ms pick default kernel immediately.
Marta: also consider split pools: keep a low-latency streaming pool with lightweight kernel selection (no sampler) and a high-throughput pool for bulk completions.
Ana: I ran a quick hack — sampler timeout 50ms for flows with streaming flag. p99 dropped to ~240ms (good improvement), p95 unchanged.
Devon: nice. any regression on throughput? 50ms early decision reduces ideal kernel picks, might increase token cost slightly.
Ana: throughput drop negligible in our canary: <1.5% token/sec change in steady runs.
Shaun: longer term we should: (a) make kernel-sampler aware of handshake/prefetch state, (b) attach mb-intent metadata (streaming vs batch) from frontend, (c) add an adaptive threshold that uses short-circuit if handshake time > threshold.
Tim: also log a new perf tag when sampler delays > 100ms: `sampler_delay_ms` so we can alert on tail regressions.
perf-bot: noted — created perf ticket #INF-472 with initial traces and p99 numbers.
Marta: small thing — KV cache behavior: streaming flows have fewer prefix tokens but more frequent small reads, so prefetch policy should keep recent KV entries hotter. we had a kv-eviction at ~2s in the canary which caused a miss spike.
Ana: yes saw KV miss bursts correlated with longer tails. adding a small-prefetch window fixed some misses.
Devon: proposed short-term plan:
- rollout sampler timeout 50ms for streaming-tagged flows (canary today)
- implement `sampler_delay_ms` metric + alert
- create a dedicated streaming pool with kernel-sampler disabled (experiment)
- improve KV prefetch TTL for streaming-heavy nodes
Shaun: agrees. what's the rollout gate? success = p99 within 1.2x baseline and throughput drop <3%.
Ana: canary data: p99 240ms (vs baseline 210ms) -> 1.14x. throughput delta +0.8%. qualifies.
Tim: ok schedule: canary->staged 24h->gradual 7d. include perf-bot smoke after each stage.
Marta: also add a small test harness for microbatch sizes: synthetic streaming workload with mbsize=1 and variable interarrival times. current loadgen misses that corner.
Ana: adding test now. will push canary patch and link the PR.
perf-bot: INF-472 updated with canary numbers and PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/pull/8342
Ops: heads-up to oncall: if sampler timeout causes increased CPU on streaming pool, revert flag. I'll watch.
Ana: thanks everyone, I'll post final canary summary in ~2h. :thumbsup:
